meeting.title: Function Health implementation catch-up
meeting.summary: Catch-up on the stalled Function Health implementation. The security review that has been blocking everything is nearly complete: Nadia is waiting on one approval from their platform lead and expects to close it out early next week. Oliver will provision the Snowflake service account (read-only on ANALYTICS, no raw layer) the same day security signs off, which unblocks the repo connection.
action_items: Nadia to close out the security review early next week (waiting on platform lead approval)
Oliver to provision the Snowflake service account (read-only, ANALYTICS schema) the same day security signs off
key_decisions: Service account scope confirmed as read-only on the ANALYTICS schema only — no access to the raw layer holding identifiable lab results
meeting.notes: The infosec and HIPAA questionnaire has been the bottleneck for three weeks. Nadia has the remaining answers drafted and is waiting on one internal approval.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Thanks for making time. I know this project has been stuck behind the security review, so I mostly want to understand where that stands.

transcript.speaker: Nadia Kaur
transcript.text: Fair. It's taken longer than any of us wanted — the questionnaire touched teams that don't usually review vendors together, and anything touching patient data gets extra scrutiny.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Understood. Is there anything outstanding on our side? More documentation, a call with your reviewers?

transcript.speaker: Nadia Kaur
transcript.text: No, your responses were complete, including the HIPAA and data-handling sections. The remaining answers are drafted internally and I'm waiting on one approval from our platform lead. I expect to close the review out early next week.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: That's genuinely good news. Oliver, once that lands, what's the path to getting us connected?

transcript.speaker: Oliver Hartley
transcript.text: The moment Nadia signs off, I'll provision the Snowflake service account — read-only on the ANALYTICS schema, exactly as specced. It's a same-day job once the review closes, so I won't put a separate date on it.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: And just to confirm scope while we're all here: read-only, ANALYTICS schema only, no raw layer?

transcript.speaker: Oliver Hartley
transcript.text: Correct. Our data governance policy won't allow raw-layer access for external tools — that's where the identifiable lab results live — and honestly you don't need it.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Agreed, we don't. Once the service account exists we can connect the dbt repo the same day, so the chain unblocks quickly.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Hartley
transcript.text: That's what I'm hoping. We've lost about three weeks; if the connection happens next week we can claw most of that back.

transcript.speaker: Nadia Kaur
transcript.text: From my side, no further reviews needed after this one. The tool itself was approved — it was the data-sharing terms for the health data that took time.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Good to know. I won't pile more actions on — the sign-off and the service account are the whole critical path. Anything you need from me?

transcript.speaker: Oliver Hartley
transcript.text: Nothing right now. If provisioning throws anything weird I'll ping you on Slack.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Perfect. Let's speak once the account is live. Thanks both.

The service account depends on that review closing, and its notes must carry the agreed scope: read-only, ANALYTICS schema only, no raw layer. Transcript fixed (Caroline's review): Oliver previously promised 'Monday the 22nd', which contradicted the review only closing early next week; he now ties it to the sign-off with no separate date.
